DR Digital Twin: A Three-Layer Deep Learning Pipeline for Diabetic Retinopathy Progression Modeling and Treatment Simulation

Hardware: NVIDIA RTX 5090 (32 GB VRAM), Intel Core i9 Ultra, 128 GB RAM

1. Pipeline Architecture

The DR Digital Twin is a three-layer pipeline that processes OCT scans through biomarker detection, temporal progression modeling, and treatment simulation to produce personalized treatment recommendations.

2. Layer 1: Multi-Label Biomarker Detection

We trained four model architectures (CNN/ResNet-18, GCN, Signed GCN, Prior-GAT) across three seeds each (42, 123, 2024) for robust evaluation. All models use the NPMI co-occurrence graph to encode biomarker relationships.

3. Layer 2: Temporal Progression & Causal Analysis

The Graph-LSTM progression model learns temporal biomarker transitions from longitudinal patient visits. From these learned dynamics, we extract a temporal causal biomarker graph using Granger causality analysis.

4. Layer 3: Treatment Simulation

The Digital Twin simulates four treatment strategies (Anti-VEGF, Steroid, Laser, Observation) for each test patient over 6 future visits, recommending the treatment with lowest predicted severity.

5. Summary

The DR Digital Twin pipeline successfully:

  • Trained 12 biomarker detection models achieving up to F1=0.806, AUROC=0.898
  • Discovered 19 significant causal edges between retinal biomarkers
  • Identified key cascade: DRT/ME -> IRF -> IRHRF
  • Generated personalized treatment recommendations for 10 test patients
  • All results from real OLIVES clinical data - no synthetic/simulated data used
